transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan, Priya Shah (Redwood); James Carter, Linda Gomez, Marcus Lee (SouthBank)

Summary:
Brief discovery focused on Dedicated capacity: reserved GPUs, isolation requirements, burst/burst-to-hosted strategy, autoscaling expectations, and security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Customer requested pricing bands and a short benchmark plan.

Topics:
- Current infra and where LLM inference runs today
- Latency and throughput SLOs, p95/p99 expectations
- Data isolation, VPC and on-prem considerations
- Burst/overflow strategy to hosted Redwood API
- Autoscaling and warm GPU pools
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we can do quick intros. I'm Alex, AE with Redwood, and Priya our SE will run through perf stuff.
[00:10] James: Hi, James Carter here — Head of ML at SouthBank. Glad to be on, we've got Linda and Marcus as well.
[00:15] Linda: Linda Gomez, CTO.
[00:17] Marcus: Marcus Lee, infra lead. Morning.
[00:20] Alex: Cool. Objective today is to understand your workloads and whether Dedicated makes sense vs hosted or private. Quick high level from you — what's the app and the constraints?
[00:30] James: We're shipping an agent-first conversational flow for customer support and fraud triage. It's multi-tenant inside our prod, but PII must not persist with third parties. So data isolation and lineage are big. Latency target is p95 < 250ms for short requests, p99 < 800ms. Throughput varies - baseline 200 rps but we see spikes up to 1k rps during payroll windows.
[00:53] Priya: Got it. When you say 200 baseline /1k peak, is that sustained or bursts over a few minutes?
[00:58] James: Typically spikes for 5-15 minutes, sometimes longer during batch jobs. We also have longer context chats that are slower.
[01:05] Alex: Sounds like a Dedicated pool with burst banding to hosted could work — Dedicated for baseline and predictable latency, and a burst policy to offload overflow to Redwood hosted if you allow outbound egress.
[01:18] Linda: We may not allow outbound for sensitive data. Can you do a Private deployment in our VPC?
[01:24] Priya: Yes, Private is an option, but it's heavier ops and licensing. Dedicated gives isolation at the tenant level — dedicated GPU pools and no model data mixing — but control plane is still Redwood managed unless you pick Private. For strict no-egress, Private or on-prem is the right call.
[01:40] Marcus: For Dedicated, what does 'isolation' mean exactly? Are the GPUs physically dedicated or just logically?
[01:47] Priya: Physically dedicated to your tenancy — GPU pools allocated to the customer, separate routing and KV caches, and separate disk volumes for any caching. There is also network isolation for traffic egress. We'll check the exact topology diagrams but that's the model.
[02:05] James: How do you handle warm starts and cold starts? Our p99 spikes are mostly due to cold KV cache misses.
[02:12] Priya: We use warm pools + intelligent pre-warming. For Dedicated you can configure minimum pool size and pre-warm policies. KV cache persists across sessions on the Dedicated nodes, so cold starts are much less frequent. There's also continuous batching to improve throughput.
[02:30] Marcus: Any details on quantizaton— I mean quantization—and which model families are supported?
[02:36] Priya: We support major open families and vet quantized variants. There's a tradeoff in quality vs cost. We generally recommend int8 quant for lower cost with broader QA. We do end-to-end evals.
[02:48] Linda: Security — SOC2 and KMS. Do you provide BYOK?
[02:52] Alex: Yes, Dedicated integrates with customer KMS (BYOK) for key wrapping. For Private we can support HSM, depending on the on-prem/hybrid setup. We are SOC2 Type II compliant and can share the report under an NDA.
[03:05] James: Good. Audit logs and data residency — we need full audit trails and retention options.
[03:10] Priya: Redwood Console exposes per-route logs, token-level cost, and tracing. We can configure audit log retention and push to your S3/GCS or SIEM. There might be a small latency/throughput impact if you enable synchronous exports.
[03:25] Marcus: What about scaling? If we provision N GPUs for Dedicated, how does autoscaling work and how fast?
[03:32] Priya: Dedicated supports vertical autoscaling via additional nodes + burst capacity. There's configurable autoscale policies (reactive and scheduled). Warm-up can be 1-5 minutes depending on model size; we also support burst-to-hosted instantly for overflow but again that's subject to egress/data policies.
[03:47] James: Suppose we need 1k rps peak. What GPU count should we expect?
[03:52] Priya: Rough estimate depends on model size and sequence length. For a 13B model at moderate sampling and 32 tokens avg, we'd estimate roughly 8-12 A100-equivalent GPUs for sustained 1k rps with batching. Priya: I'll produce a calc doc with numbers for 7B, 13B, and 70B variants.
[04:10] Alex: We'll also share a benchmark spreadsheet where you can plug in your seq lengths and sampling.
[04:16] Linda: How does reserved vs burst billing work? If we reserve capacity, can we burst to hosted and only pay for burst usage?
[04:24] Alex: Yes, billing is a combination. Reserved Dedicated gives you a flat commit (monthly/annual) for baseline. Burst-to-hosted is usage-based; we can model a blended rate for budgeting. There's also option for committed + overage hours at a reduced incremental rate.
[04:40] Marcus: Are there network egress concerns if we do burst-to-hosted? We route traffic inside our VPC today.
[04:46] Priya: Burst-to-hosted would traverse Redwood's control plane unless you use private peering. For high-security, customers use Private Deploy or set up dedicated peering with strict egress rules. We'll note that in the sec deep dive.
[04:58] James: What about model rollouts — can we pin model versions and canary?
[05:02] Priya: Yes, rollouts and canary routing is supported in Dedicated via the Console. You can do A/B by route or percentage. Also automatic fallback to smaller model variants if capacity constrained.
[05:14] Linda: Do you support on-prem option for air-gapped deployments?
[05:17] Alex: Yes, Private on-prem is supported but it's a different engagement with infra ops and licensing. Good fit if you can't have any external egress or require local-only data.
[05:26] James: For benchmarking, we'd like to run a short POC. Can you propose a minimal pilot?
[05:30] Alex: Typically a 2-4 week pilot: we provision a small Dedicated pool (1-4 GPUs), run your trace or synthetic load, measure latency/throughput and quality. Priya can run evals and a QA pass with your prompt set.
[05:40] Priya: For data we can do anonymized traces. Also we do prompt engineering to identify token counts and memory usage. We recommend starting with 2 GPUs with warm pre-warm to validate p95 and throughput.
[05:52] Marcus: If the pilot shows we need 12 GPUs, what's the lead time to scale Dedicated?
[05:57] Priya: We typically can scale within 24-72 hours to add nodes subject to inventory. For large scale (10s of GPUs) might need longer lead time. We can also provision burst capacity quicker via hosted.
[06:10] James: Any gotchas around KV cache eviction or multi-tenant cache coldness?
[06:15] Priya: With Dedicated you get your own KV cache, eviction policy can be tuned, and you can pin prefixes. In hosted multitenant, you see more coldness due to sharing. We sometimes see transcription errors in docs where KV cache shows as 'KV cash' in exports — but it's cache.
[06:30] Linda: Compliance wise, can you support our security questionnaire?
[06:33] Alex: Yes, we have a security pack — SOC2 reports, penetration test summary, encryption and key management details. We'll share the PDF via secure link.
[06:42] James: Are there customers similar to us in fintech using Dedicated?
[06:45] Alex: Yes, several banks and fintechs run Dedicated — examples we can share (anonymized) in a case study.
[06:52] Marcus: Latency SLA — do you offer SLA-backed p95 numbers?
[06:56] Alex: For Dedicated we can include latency and uptime SLAs in enterprise agreements. Exact numbers depend on commit and topology.
[07:04] Linda: We also need RBAC and SSO integration.
[07:07] Priya: Console supports SAML SSO and role-based access controls. Some customers map roles to their AD groups.
[07:15] James: Ok let's recap what we need from you and what we'll provide.
[07:19] Alex: From our side: pricing band, Dedicated baseline vs burst pricing, benchmark spreadsheet, security pack, and a pilot proposal.
[07:26] Marcus: From us: 2 weeks of traces, confirmation on egress policy, and legal contact for SOC2.
[07:32] Linda: Also timeline — we aim to decide by end of Q2, want pilot in April.
[07:36] Alex: Sounds good. We'll get materials over early next week.
[07:40] James: One more question — how do you handle model updates and versioning with dedicated? Will new model weights be pushed automatically?
[07:48] Priya: Model updates are controlled — you can pin to versions and we support managed upgrades with canaries. We won't push breaking changes without coordination.
[07:56] Alex: Great. Any other blockers?
[07:58] Marcus: Licensing/contracting needs to go through our procurement but no blockers on tech.
[08:02] Linda: We'll wait for the security docs.
[08:05] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with next steps.

End meeting.
